decisions.executionNote: Begin elbow-up approach to the rear left tube, lifting and pitching the left wrist; right arm remains home.
Advance left arm over the rear-left tube while aligning the downward gripper with its diagonal axis.
Lower and complete diagonal alignment over the first tube; retain open fingers until centered.
Fine-align to the tube axis and close the left fingers around its upper body.
Wrist view shows remaining axial skew; reopen briefly and correct yaw before regrasping.
Release and lift clear before correcting yaw, avoiding rotating the tube through finger contact.
Recenter over the tube's new resting position from head and wrist views, then descend with fingers fully open.
Shift grip toward the cap for insertion clearance, close fully, and start a small retention-check lift.
Lift the retained tube clear of the table with a small retreat before making it upright.
Tube remains in the fingers; begin a gradual upright rotation while carrying toward the left rack slot.
Continue the smooth upright rotation and transfer, keeping the tube above the rack.
Finish making the tube upright and approach the left front rack slot from above; inspect alignment before insertion.
Lower the upright first tube into the left-front hole with a small rightward centering correction.
Seat the first tube farther into the slot and release it, then inspect its stability and depth.
Withdraw open fingers to inspect whether the first tube remains upright and seated in its hole.
The first tube did not stay seated; clear the rack area to locate it and plan a corrected recovery.
Approach the remaining left-side tube with a gradual downward wrist orientation; the fallen tube remains visible for later recovery.
Continue the elbow-up approach, rotating toward a top-down grasp of the left tube.
Complete downward alignment above the second left tube before descending.
Use wrist-camera centering to shift toward the tube and lower with fingers open.
Center the second tube between the fingers, descend to grasp height, close fully, and test retention with a short lift.
Lift the second tube clear; retain the closed grasp before rotating upright for a visually aligned insertion.
Begin upright rotation and transfer above the left rack region, using a simpler forward-facing final wrist alignment.
Continue upright transfer; keep the tube securely closed and above the rack.
Finish the upright orientation and stop above the left slot for visual alignment.
Correct the rejected tensor: expose the tube for alignment while preserving its horizontal position and approaching the rack surface.
Lower slowly with the grasp maintained, checking the rack and tube alignment before releasing.
Continue a slow vertical insertion attempt without opening; compare tube and rack motion to detect seating or rim contact.
Tube stopped descending at the rack rim; keep it held and shift slightly left and forward to center its tip over the hole.
After centering over the left hole, lower slowly again while retaining the tube.
Complete the shallow final seating motion, then open the fingers without disturbing the tube.
Withdraw the open left gripper upward and back to verify that the tube remains seated.
The left tube remains upright in the rack. Clear the left arm while starting an elbow-up approach to the right tube.
Continue returning the left arm while moving the right gripper above its tube and aligning with the tube axis.
Finish returning the left arm and bring the right gripper into its top-down pregrasp above the right tube.
Center and lower the right gripper toward its tube; left arm settles at home.
Descend and grasp the right tube near its upper body, then lift slightly to check retention.
Lift the right tube clear of the tabletop while keeping the grasp closed.
Begin gradual upright rotation while carrying the right tube toward the rightmost rack hole.
Continue carrying and rotating the retained right tube toward an upright insertion approach.
Finish making the right tube upright above the right-front hole, then inspect before lowering.
Center the upright right tube slightly left and forward, and lower toward its rack opening while keeping it held.
Continue lowering the upright right tube into its opening, maintaining the grasp to check depth before release.
The right tube appears to contact the rim; lift slightly and shift right to align its vertical axis with the opening.
Lower the newly centered right tube slowly to seating depth, still holding it.
The tube has not descended fully; relieve contact and move its tip forward into the opening, then lower gently again.
The right tube is now centered above the opening; open in place so it can settle into the slot without further finger contact.
Withdraw the open right gripper to verify seating, while beginning the left arm's elbow-up recovery approach to the fallen tube.
Both seated tubes remain in the rack. Return the right arm and advance the left arm above the fallen tube, keeping elbows up.
Bring the left gripper downward above the fallen tube while gradually turning to face its reversed cap direction; continue the right-arm return.
